review_candidates.title: Investment Manager – Renewable Energy Finance
review_candidates.description: Bouw mee aan de financiering van de Europese energietransitie Zonhub is een toonaangevende, gereguleerde Nederlandse fintech in de financiering van duurzame energie-infrastructuur. We hebben inmiddels meer dan €160 miljoen aan duurzame energieprojecten gefinancierd, verdeeld over ruim 300 projecten en ondersteund door meer dan 13.000 investeerders. Nu zetten we de volgende stap: we breiden uit naar nieuwe Europese markten, met de ambitie om voor meer dan €500 miljoen aan duurzame energieprojecten te financieren. Als Investment Manager structureer en begeleid je financieringen van €250.000 tot €5 miljoen. Je werkt rechtstreeks met projectontwikkelaars, energiebedrijven en professionele investeerders en bent van analyse tot closing verantwoordelijk voor succesvolle transacties. Dit is nadrukkelijk geen juniorfunctie : je bent een ondernemende deal professional die steeds zelfstandiger transacties leidt. Waarom deze rol? Veel eigen verantwoordelijkheid en directe verantwoordelijkheid voor transacties; Werk aan de financiering van zonne-, wind- en batterijopslagprojecten; Intensief contact met ondernemers, investeerders en institutionele financiers; Een sleutelrol in de Europese groeifase van Zonhub. Wat je gaat doen Structureer duurzame energie-financieringen van circa €250.000 tot €5 miljoen; Begeleid transacties van eerste analyse tot closing; Je werk direct samen met projectontwikkelaars en energiebedrijven; Ontwikkel financiële modellen, term sheets en investeringsmemoranda; Coördineer due diligence en interne besluitvorming; Bouw duurzame klantrelaties op en draag bij aan commerciële groei; Denk mee over nieuwe proposities en schaalbare processen. Wat wij bieden Een sleutelrol binnen een gevestigde, gereguleerde fintech met Europese groeiambities; Directe impact op de energietransitie; Veel autonomie en verantwoordelijkheid; Een professioneel, ondernemend en internationaal team; Een dienstverband van 32–40 uur per week; Marktconform salaris, pensioenregeling en goede secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden Hybride werken en een centraal kantoor in Amsterdam. Wat je meebrengt Minimaal twee jaar relevante ervaring in projectfinanciering, corporate finance, banking, investment management of duurzame energie; hbo-/wo-werk- en denkniveau; Sterk analytisch, met commercieel inzicht en gevoel voor relaties; Ondernemend, zelfstandig en resultaatgericht; Uitstekende beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal. Werken bij Zonhub Bij Zonhub mobiliseren we kapitaal voor een van de grootste vraagstukken van onze tijd. Als onafhankelijk en gereguleerd financieringsplatform combineren we de snelheid en ondernemingszin van een fintech met de professionaliteit van een financiële instelling — en krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, dicht op de transacties. Solliciteren Interesse? We ontvangen graag je motivatiebrief en recente cv. Reageer via de “Solliciteer nu” button; Vragen over de rol? Mail Shari Karodia via shari@zonhub.com; Screening maakt onderdeel uit van onze sollicitatieprocedure. Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

review_candidates.title: Investment Analyst
review_candidates.description: JOB PURPOSE (For Omani Only) Support the evaluation of real estate development projects by contributing to the structuring, assessment, and refinement of investment cases, supporting investment decision-making, and assisting in engagement with sub-developers, investors, and partners to ensure alignment with commercial, financial, and strategic objectives. KEY ROLES & RESPONSIBILITIES Support the evaluation of real estate development projects or portfolios, from initial assessment through internal approvals. Prepare and maintain financial models, feasibility analyses, and investment cases to support development opportunities by the master developer and by local and international sub-developers and investors. Prepare investment memoranda, executive summaries, investor presentations, and related materials. Support business development activities, including the identification and evaluation of sub-developers, investors, and capital providers. Assist with deal structuring and execution, including development strategies, phasing plans, financing structures, and transaction closing. Support the evaluation of transactions involving land sales, land leases, joint ventures, and other collaboration structures, and assist in developing recommendations for decision-making. Assist in preparing commercial input for term sheets, MOUs, sale and purchase agreements, and other transaction and partnership frameworks, in coordination with legal and other internal teams. Support engagement with sub-developers, investors, capital providers, advisors, and service providers. Monitor market developments and contribute market intelligence and sector insights, ensuring the department remains informed of relevant trends locally, regionally, and internationally. Contribute to the continuous improvement of investment processes, systems, documentation, and record-keeping, in line with best practices and efficiency objectives. MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, or a related field. 1 to 3 years of relevant experience in real estate investment, development, feasibility analysis, corporate finance, or a related field. Professional certifications such as CFA, CAIA, FMVA, or equivalent are strongly preferred. Fluency in English is essential. Proficiency in MS Office, particularly MS Excel and MS PowerPoint.

review_candidates.title: Cost Control Manager - Projects
review_candidates.description: Role Overview The Cost Control Manager – Projects is responsible for overseeing project cost management, budgeting, forecasting, and financial performance across real estate development and construction projects. The role ensures that project expenditures remain aligned with approved budgets, identifies cost variances and potential financial risks, and provides accurate cost reporting to support informed decision-making. This position works closely with Project Management, Development, Procurement, Contracts, Finance, and Consultants to maintain cost discipline throughout the project lifecycle, from design and procurement through construction, handover, and closeout. 2. Key Responsibilities Project Cost Management Develop, implement, and maintain project cost control procedures, systems, and reporting standards. Establish project cost baselines based on approved budgets, project scope, schedules, and contractual commitments. Monitor actual costs, commitments, accruals, and forecast costs against approved budgets. Identify cost overruns, budget deviations, and potential financial risks, recommending corrective actions. Maintain accurate cost breakdown structures (CBS) and cost reports across assigned projects. Budgeting and Forecasting Lead the preparation and review of project budgets, cost plans, and periodic cost forecasts. Monitor project cost performance and estimate the cost to complete (ETC) and estimate at completion (EAC). Conduct variance analysis and provide explanations for significant deviations from approved budgets. Support budget revisions, contingency planning, and financial impact assessments arising from changes in project scope. Ensure alignment between project budgets, procurement plans, construction schedules, and contractual commitments. Change and Contract Cost Control Review change orders, variation requests, claims, and other commercial adjustments to assess their financial impact. Monitor commitments under construction contracts, purchase orders, and consultant agreements. Coordinate with Contracts and Commercial teams to evaluate cost implications and maintain accurate forecasts. Track contingency utilization and ensure proposed changes follow the appropriate approval process. Identify opportunities for cost optimization without compromising quality, safety, or project delivery requirements. Reporting and Performance Analysis Prepare periodic cost reports, dashboards, and management summaries for project leadership. Provide clear visibility into budget utilization, committed costs, forecast final costs, and financial exposure. Develop cost performance indicators and early-warning mechanisms for projects at risk of exceeding budget. Present cost trends, risks, and mitigation plans to senior management and relevant stakeholders. Ensure the accuracy, consistency, and timeliness of project cost data. Stakeholder Management and Governance Work closely with Project Directors, Project Managers, Development teams, Finance, Procurement, and Consultants. Establish consistent cost control practices across multiple projects and project teams. Ensure compliance with approved budgets, delegated authorities, financial controls, and reporting requirements. Support project audits, financial reviews, and project closeout activities. Lead and develop the project cost control team, ensuring accountability and high-quality deliverables. 3. Qualifications and Experience Bachelor's degree in Quantity Surveying, Engineering, Construction Management, Finance, or a related field. A master's degree in Construction Management, Project Management, or a relevant discipline is an advantage. 8–12 years of relevant experience in project cost control, cost management, or commercial management within real estate development, construction, or infrastructure projects. At least 3 years in a managerial or leadership role overseeing project cost control activities. Proven experience managing budgets, cost forecasts, commitments, variations, and financial reporting for large-scale development or construction projects. Experience working with developers, project management consultancies, contractors, or program management organizations is preferred. Strong knowledge of construction contracts, cost estimation, quantity surveying principles, and project financial controls. 4. Technical Skills Project budgeting, cost planning, forecasting, and variance analysis. Cost-to-complete and estimate-at-completion methodologies. Change management, variation assessment, and claims cost evaluation. Construction cost breakdown structures and commitment tracking. Advanced Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint. Proficiency in cost management and project controls systems such as Primavera P6, SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms. Familiarity with Power BI and project cost dashboards is an advantage. Understanding of earned value management (EVM) and project performance measurement. 5. Key Competencies Analytical thinking and financial acumen. Leadership and team management. Stakeholder management and influencing skills. Commercial awareness and risk management. Attention to detail and data accuracy. Problem-solving and decision-making. Strong communication and executive reporting skills. Ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities. 6. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) Accuracy of project cost forecasts and estimates at completion. Timeliness and accuracy of periodic cost reports. Percentage of projects maintained within approved budgets. Early identification and escalation of cost overruns and financial risks. Effectiveness of change order and variation cost assessments. Reduction in unplanned cost overruns and budget deviations. Compliance with project cost control procedures and governance requirements. Effective utilization of contingency budgets and cost optimization opportunities. 7. Stakeholder Relationships Internal: Project Directors, Project Managers, Development, Finance, Procurement, Contracts, Commercial, and Risk Management. External: Project Management Consultants, Cost Consultants, Contractors, Engineering Consultants, and other relevant project stakeholders
